title: Normalized open tensor data on arbitrary one-K-flat representatives
statement: For two small ringed sites $(C,J,R)$ and $(C',J',R')$ in a common size bound [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], use their ordinary unbounded derived categories and recorded internal Homs [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], closed tensor structures $A,A'$ and simultaneous K-flat models $T,T'$ [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Use actual sheafified module tensors, pure sections and signed direct-sum total tensors [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Fix exact additive module functors $F:\operatorname{Mod}(R')\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $G:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R')$, an adjunction $F\dashv G$, a site functor $H:C\to C'$, and specified section pull maps $N(V)\to(GN)(HV)$. Define normalized open tensor representative data, relative to these parameters, to consist of: (i) a derived restriction/tensor isomorphism with its ordinary, signed-chain, K-flat and derived representative models, whose ordinary map carries pulled-back pure tensors to the pure tensor of the pulled-back sections; (ii) ordinary isomorphisms $FM\otimes N\cong F(M\otimes GN)$ whose inverses have adjoint transpose $(\eta_M\otimes1)$ followed by the inverse restriction/tensor comparison; (iii) chain isomorphisms $\operatorname{Tot}(FC\otimes P)\cong F\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes GP)$ whose restriction to every $(a,b)$ signed total summand is the ordinary comparison; (iv) the existing natural one-K-flat tensor comparisons on both sites, agreeing with $T,T'$ [def-zl-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal-data], and preservation by $G$ of flat terms on flat-term K-flat complexes; (v) a whole-derived natural isomorphism $\gamma:FM\otimes^LN\cong F(M\otimes^LGN)$ with the adjoint-unit inverse normalization [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], whose value on every arbitrary complex $C$ and flat-term K-flat $P$ is the localization of the chain map in (iii) through the comparisons in (iv). This defines data only, without asserting its existence for arbitrary $F,G$. For the actual open adjunction the specified section pull is the inverse-image unit; on a sequence site all chain maps are module morphisms on the full site, hence include its horizontal semilinear restrictions.

lean.note: Pure data packaging the normalized-open representative clauses. Existing one-K-flat tensor-comparison definitions are reused, not redefined; existence is stated only by the owning compact-support/open-model theorem. H4 interface diagnosis: lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization's Mode.systems Assertion.gamma is relative to Operations.tensorX/tensorU of ProjectionRestriction.TensorModel. That type supplies a bifunctor and simultaneous resolving-pair representative/descent data only; it is not the CoefficientClosedStructure with the prescribed internal Hom and CoefficientTensorModels used by CoefficientDerivedSystemTensors, and provides no conversion to those fixed structures or one-K-flat comparison for an arbitrary first complex. Its restrictRing, open restriction and chosen extension also use the localized-site presentation rather than the native varying-ring pull/extension functors. Thus Assertion.gamma cannot directly be used at the required tensor and functor types. OpenTensorModel is the representative refinement at those recorded native interfaces, not a second definition of tensor: restrictionPure fixes the ordinary restriction comparison, ordinary_inverse and summand fix its signed total representative, and derived_model fixes its localization. gamma_inverse is exactly Assertion.gamma_inverse's open-unit adjoint transpose, using the same exactDerivedAdjunction. Under representative-preserving tensor and open-adjunction comparisons the inverse transposes agree, hence adjunction injectivity identifies the transported gamma with Assertion.gamma. The source normalization and all unbounded inputs are retained without assuming equality of independently presented tensor functors.
